title_ko: 경복궁 사정전 <쌍룡도> 벽화의 설치 배경과 제작 시기 검토
title_en: A Study on the Origin and Production Date of the Twin Dragon Painting of Sajeongjeon Hall in Gyeongbokgung Palace
scope: Building-specific study of the mural, its support and alteration history, including comparisons with other court interiors. Selected relevant pages checked; no complete article review or primary archive verification claimed.
relevance: Separates the history of the painted image from its architectural mounting; helps interpret the central assembly in the 1993 drawings and later display photographs.

notes.statement: Park reports conservation in 1986 and removal of the painting and its detachable framed support in 2000; a photographic facsimile replaced it. The removal photographs show the support being lowered between the tall internal columns.
notes.scope: An account based on conservation documentation; dates of the painted image and its support are separate questions.

evidence.locator_note: Section II.1, conservation history and figure 3 (1986 photographs).
Figure 4 and text describing the 2000 removal, frame construction and photographic replacement.

notes.review_note: Agent read the cited passages and inspected full-page renders, including captions and surrounding qualifications, on 2026-09-21. Checked means an accurate reading of this source; its primary evidence and proposed historical reconstruction have not been independently verified.

notes.statement: Park connects traces on the central columns and beams with a former screen or opening below the upper painted panel. Figure 11 records these traces; the proposed operable lower enclosure is an interpretation, not a surviving complete mechanism.
notes.scope: Candidate relationship for the central bay; Chinese palace comparisons do not establish identical construction in Sajeongjeon.

evidence.locator_note: Paragraphs above/beside figure 11 and its three detail photographs.

notes.statement: Park argues that the mounting belongs to the rebuilding-era arrangement while the surviving painting is later, probably associated with the colonial exhibition/museum period. The conclusion remains a historical argument; its dated photographs and conservation records are leads for independent checking.
notes.scope: Selected argument/conclusion checked; the complete stylistic comparison and original backing-paper decipherment were not independently repeated.
